We need to create a non-negative sequence of coefficients that minimizes the score defined in the objective function. The previous program only tried constant sequences, which converges to a score of 2 (due to the way convolution is defined). We will instead use a more sophisticated approach based on polynomial sequences, which need not be constant. The idea is to generate candidate sequences by varying the degrees of polynomials, use simulated annealing to optimize the sequence, and maintain the best candidate throughout the search.

We expect that using polynomial sequences (which are smooth and allow variation) will help us achieve better results than constant sequences. The score is defined as 2*n*max(convolve(a, a)) / (sum(a)^2). Polynomial sequences can be designed to have controlled autocorrelation properties, potentially leading to lower scores.

We leverage accurate gradient descent and consider sequences of different lengths (128, 256, and 512) to see if longer sequences yield better results. We also apply the "leader-follower" strategy in the reconstruction stage to avoid the trailing edges of the step function having the maximum value.

We'll use a uniform step increase for the candidate evaluation. The optimization algorithm will be simulated annealing, using exact gradients.
